$schema_note: Acknowledged `supabase migration repair` placeholder rows, per target. Read by scripts/migration-rehearsal/check-migration-safety.mjs -- and read out of git's object store at HEAD, never from the working tree, so an untracked, symlinked, or hardlinked file at this path cannot substitute for the reviewed blob. A placeholder row is one with statements IS NULL: it asserts a version is applied without recording what content was applied, so history stops being proof of what is live. Listing a VERSION here means a human already reconciled that version against the live schema and accepts it as baseline noise. Contents are deliberately NOT recorded -- a placeholder has none. Adding entries must be a reviewed commit, never a runtime flag, so an automated loop cannot acknowledge the very row that should have stopped it.
$how_to_extend: Run the gate. If it refuses with E21 it prints a paste-ready array containing the existing baseline plus the new versions. Confirm each new version against the live schema first (e.g. pg_get_functiondef on the objects that migration touches), then paste, set acknowledged_at, and COMMIT. An uncommitted edit has no effect: the gate reads HEAD.
$identity_keys: project_ref is matched exactly against PGUSER (postgres.<ref>) or PGHOST (db.<ref>.supabase.co), never as a substring. database is compared to PGDATABASE and to the live current_database(). db_system_identifier is the cluster's pg_control_system().system_identifier. Every key must be present AND non-null: a null identity field does NOT disable the check, it fails the run closed (E06). Unbound targets are reachable only under the gate's --test-mode, which guarded-db-push.sh cannot pass, so no target in this file can ever authorise a push without full identity. Caveat on db_system_identifier: it identifies a cluster lineage, so a physical restore or byte clone preserves it and a logical branch gets a new one -- it is a fail-closed operational signal, not complete identity proof, and it is one of three independent bindings.
$no_test_targets: This file deliberately contains no unbound or test target. An earlier revision shipped a 'local-rehearsal' entry with null identity fields, which -- combined with null meaning 'skip the check' -- was a committed bypass: guarded-db-push.sh --target=local-rehearsal would have run against production with identity verification disabled. Both halves of that are fixed; do not reintroduce either.
